summary: António de Spínola (1910–1996), a cavalry general who had governed Portuguese Guinea and commanded there from 1968 to 1973, published Portugal e o Futuro in February 1974 arguing that the colonial war had no military solution. Dismissed with Costa Gomes in March, he was accepted by the Armed Forces Movement as the public face of the 25 April coup and became the first president of the new republic. He wanted a federal solution for the African territories and a slower, more presidential transition; the movement wanted independence and a faster one. He resigned after the confrontation of 28 September 1974, attempted to reverse the course on 11 March 1975, and went into exile. He is in the atlas because two of the period's turning points are his defeats.
